questions: If multiple subarrays have the same minimal length, should we output any one length or is there a tie‑breaking rule required?
Should the subarray be required to contain at least two occurrences of the same value, or is a single occurrence considered a “repeated value” if that value appears elsewhere in the whole array?
Are subarrays defined as contiguous segments of the original sequence, or can they be any subsequence (not necessarily contiguous)?
If no subarray satisfying the condition exists, what should be printed (e.g., -1, 0, or a specific message)?
Must the repeated value appear at least twice within the chosen subarray itself, or is it sufficient that the value appears elsewhere in the array outside the subarray?
Are there any constraints on the size of the output integer (e.g., should it fit in 32‑bit signed integer) or formatting requirements (e.g., newline after the number)?
Can the input contain leading or trailing whitespace, multiple spaces between numbers, or line breaks after each A_i, and should the program handle such formatting?
Is N guaranteed to match the actual count of provided A_i values, or should the program validate and handle mismatched input lengths?

inline_prompts: You are given a positive integer N and an integer sequence A = (A_1,A_2,\dots,A_N) of length N. Determine whether there exists a non-empty subarray of A that has a repeated value, occurring multiple times in A. If such a subarray exists, find the length of the shortest such subarray. Any solution with the minimum stair count is acceptable; tie-breaking is not required. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output print the length of the shortest such subarray. Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq A_i \leq 10^6 \ (1 \leq i \leq N) - All input values are integers.
